claim: The composition of library-2 LNP #54 (lipomer 58 / spermidine+lauryl acrylate, DOPE, 10:1, C14 PEG, PEG MW 2000, diameter 31.2 nm)
locus_a: SI Fig S4f p20, endothelial-cell sub-table: Lipomer Mole % = 36 (with cholesterol 60, PEG 5, helper 0 -> sums to 101)
locus_b: SI Fig S3d p12 LNP #54 AND SI Fig S4f p20's own MACROPHAGE sub-table, same particle, same 31.2 nm diameter: Lipomer Mole % = 35 (sums to 100)
what_we_emitted: Nothing (0 corpus rows). 01_design_tables.csv carries 35 as read from Fig S3d; 02_rank_tables.csv carries the 36 verbatim as printed and 03_checks.json flags it as the single 101% row.
why: The four mole percents summing to 100 is a constraint the authors imposed on all 564 design rows and never printed, so it is external to both printings and decides between them: 35+60+5+0=100, 36+60+5+0=101. Two of the three printings say 35. We do not silently correct a published number, so the extraction keeps what each locus prints and the contradiction is recorded here. This is also the only one of 87 rank rows that fails the invariant (check B2: 86/87 at exactly 100).

claim: The size of the in vitro ranking axis in Fig S4d
locus_a: SI Fig S4 caption p18: 'The columns are sorted from best (LNP 1) to worst (LNP 104) in vitro'
locus_b: Main text P11 and SI Fig S3h/i: the stable pools are 112 (library 1), 105 (library 2) and 64 (library 3) -- none of them 104
why: One caption sentence covers three per-library panels with three different pool sizes, so no single 'worst' index can be right for all of them. 104 is nearest library 2's 105. Harmless for us because we emit no rank, but it means the caption cannot be used to infer a library's pool size.

claim: That the Fig S4e/f/g rows are the 'top 10%' in vivo
locus_a: SI Fig S4d y-axis label: 'LNP Rank in vivo (top 10%)', and the Fig S4 caption calls Fig S4e-g 'the compositions and diameters of the coloured LNPs in Fig. S4D'
locus_b: The listed counts: library 1 lists 10 of 112 stable (8.9%), library 2 lists 6 of 105 (5.7%), library 3 lists 6 of 64 (9.4%)
what_we_emitted: Nothing. 05_values.csv states on every in vivo row that the rank is CENSORED and that a blank means 'outside the listed set', not 'not measured'.
why: 'Top 10%' is a label, not the selection rule actually applied: library 2's six listed particles are the top 5.7%, which is nearly half the stated fraction. Any reader treating the blanks as a 10% cut would mis-set the censoring threshold by a factor of ~2 for library 2.

claim: Which epoxide goes with which lipomer in the SI reaction scheme
locus_a: SI Fig S2a p7 / Fig S3f p13 print 'R1=C10' above 'R2=C13', while the adjacent key prints '7C1' above '104' -- read in parallel this pairs 7C1 with R1=C10, and 7C1 is the C15 epoxide whose alkyl substituent is C13
locus_b: The colour key, measured: the 'R1=C10' band and the '104' band are RGB (250,190,159), identical at distance 0.00; the 'R2=C13' band and the '7C1' band are RGB (252,228,214), identical at distance 0.00; the cross distances are 66.88
what_we_emitted: Nothing, and NO CONTRADICTION. Retracted after measurement.
why: Recorded because I raised it and it is wrong. Reading the two stacked boxes in parallel order suggests an inversion; the boxes are colour-keyed, not order-keyed, and the colours pair 104 with R1=C10 and 7C1 with R2=C13, which is chemically correct (a 'Cn epoxy' has a C(n-2) alkyl substituent). SI Fig S5a independently confirms it: there the only epoxide is C12-Epoxy and the only R printed is 'R1=C10'. Kept in this file so the next reader does not re-raise it.
